corrected_from_the_list: a: Ctrl is tested before Alt, so Ctrl with Alt pans. Meta held does nothing. Vertical sign differs: Ctrl uses up minus down, plain rotation down minus up. Note 39 also speaks of the Alt branch.

d: Also geospatial-camera-controls.ts reads camera.limits live (lines 140, 322, 348) for zoom requests, but the final write still clamps against the closure object. Fields of the held object, including pitchDisabledRadiusScale, work.
f: Pitch is clamped (line 244) against the radius as passed in, before the radius clamp. The setters compare against the stored clamped value, not the last value written.
g: Pointer move ignores button, buttons, pointerType and pointerId. Any pointerup ends the drag. Turn needs a scene hook.
b: _applyCameraViewport in camera.ts also does not clamp.
e: A beta outside 0 to PI puts the eye on the opposite side while up stays fixed.

wrong_about_the_library: ticket-a: the branch line numbers were one off (Ctrl 117-125, Alt 127-131, plain 133-138), and so were the modifier and blur lines (58-60, 75-79, 99-104, listener 143). It also left out a branch: a direction key pressed while Meta is held is never added to the held set (line 83).

ticket-c: it said the drawn rectangle is resolveCameraViewport's clamped one. In fact the render passes use _applyCameraViewport (camera.ts 242-253; render-task-base.ts 566, geometry-renderer-task.ts 897), which uses the raw fields with no clamp. resolveCameraViewport serves picking and gizmo dragging. I rewrote the 'misleads' section to match.

ticket-d: it said controls line 140 reads limits for a zoom request. Line 140 is the picking sphere's planetRadius. The zoom reads are at 322-338 and 348-358, and line 393 was missing. Clamp lines corrected to 243-245.

ticket-e: it said any beta outside 0 to PI makes sin(beta) negative. A probe shows that beta -4 gives positive sin and the eye on the +X side. It also left out the setters (160-178): they store a changed value as given and clamp only through the hook that setCameraLimits installs; an equal write does nothing.
ticket-f: _setOrientation is put on the camera at line 291, not 286. Added the normalizeRadians line (82).

ticket-g: it left out that the rotation is applied only when an accumulator is non-zero, and that the epsilon is camera.speed*0.001. It also did not say that the doc comment (lines 5-16) claims pointer-lock, which the code does not have.
